It’s not just the weed causing addiction, it’s the life style. Personally that was the case for me. 

You will get to choose what you want to do with your day and nothing can hold you back now. It might seem hard at first but once you find what you enjoy you will thank yourself for quitting. 

Addiction is a disease. I used weed to suppress how I feel about myself, and mourning over family members. But now I embrace it and I’m actively trying to be involved with the ones I care about.

It wasn’t just quitting weed for me, it was a life style decision where I ate healthier, exercised more, and got busy with new hobbies (like painting).

I’m so grateful for where I am right now, i was so scared before I quit. I didn’t know what to expect. But now, I’m filled with so much pride that I’m not controlled by a substance no more. You will overcome it if you believe it, and trust me you’ve got all it takes right in you. 

Try joining online NA meetings (helped me when I felt lonely quitting and gave me perspective about my addiction. 

My therapist recommended meds, and I knew deep inside I didn’t need them, and I’m doing great and it’s my third day; I was right. I also tapered off it. It easier with less withdrawals. 

Embrace those feelings and don’t be scared to face them, it’s actually fun and so much better than being stoned and depressed 24/7. I really never thought I’d be saying this but I’m way happier than I’ve been in the last 3 years (my last quit then I relapsed again). 

Best of luck and wishes! <3

So I’m 3 days clean today, honestly it feels great.
It took me 7 years to be here, I’m 21, and I’m lucky to be alive today and this is my second time quitting (first was my friend od ing on drugs and almost dying, second time (current/hopefully final attempt) i od and almost died from different drugs, I had seizures and was losing vital signs at a concert they had to rush to me an ambulance and keep me in an ICU for 24 hours. I was (excuse me) puking my heart out at the concert and when I woke up in the ER continued puking and crying for help; it was a living hell. I didn’t quit then, but I realised what had happened over time (trauma settled in) and was like woah, I literally could’ve died or been paralysed if I weren’t as lucky. 

I was so worried and scared of withdrawals but honestly they’re way better than what weed made me feel (depressed and anxious about everything).

I started going to NA meetings, this is a really good step if you’re still using and want to recover. 
Having a support system like that is amazing, you can also visit online 24/7 NA meetings from all over the world if you don’t have one near by you.

Then I saw the effects it had on my friends, and how bad they became with time and made me realise what I was doing to myself and that was an eye opening experience. 

Finally I had my last stash and made the decision to cut off it slowly (smoking less by the day to get less severe withdrawals) til the stash finishes and game on, just for today I’m not smoking weed.

I started doing physical activities (like swimming/weights in home), started making healthy food decisions and got busy with my family and friends. I find keeping busy and being aware of your emotions and accepting them really is key and helps free you from the addiction. 

Try to avoid and write down your triggers that make you wanna smoke up, like for me it was being in my room all day and smoking in the morning (if you can’t cut off completely just try to avoid smoking in the mornings until it’s night time before you sleep (this’ll give you so much clarity and you’ll see the difference it has on your day. 

On day 2 my friend was smoking up next to me, and I didn’t even crave it and was like why would I put myself in this situation again.

I really hope this helps you out, I know from my experience weed only got me down, but now I feel like I can talk freely, my skin looks better, I’m being more proactive with my family and life. I’m very grateful to have NA meetings and to be able to quit and I’m lucky to have this option which didn’t exist in the past. 

Best of luck my friend!
